source.title: On the Number and the Geometry of Hyperbolic Knots and Links with a Common Cyclic Branched Covering: Known Results and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed orientable hyperbolic 3-manifold and let p be a fixed prime. Determine how many pairwise different knots and links in S^3 can have M as their p-fold cyclic branched covering, and describe how any such knots or links are related to one another.

evidence.quote: Problem 1.1: Given a closed orientable hyperbolic 3-manifold M and fixing a prime p, of how many different knots and links in the 3-sphere can M be a p-fold cyclic branched covering, and how are such knots or links related?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold. For how many distinct primes p can there exist a knot K in S^3 such that M is the p-fold cyclic branched covering of K? When this happens for several primes, how are the corresponding knots related? Is there a uniform upper bound on the number of such primes, and which finite groups can occur as isometry groups of a hyperbolic 3-manifold with this property?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1: Given a closed hyperbolic 3-manifold M, for how many different primes p can M be a p-fold cyclic branched covering of a knot K in S^3, and how are these knots related? In particular, is there an upper bound on the number of such primes p? What are the possible isometry groups of a hyperbolic 3-manifold which is a p-fold cyclic branched covering?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a hyperbolic 3-manifold that is a p-fold cyclic branched covering of a knot in S^3. Which non-solvable finite groups can occur as the isometry group of M?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4: What are the possible non-solvable isometry groups of an hyperbolic 3-manifold M which is a p-fold cyclic branched covering of a knot in S^3?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a mod 2 homology 3-sphere, and let G be a finite non-solvable group of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of M. Theorem 2.6 states that, after quotienting by the maximal normal odd-order subgroup O(G), the group G/O(G) has a normal subgroup, with factor group abelian or a 2-fold extension of an abelian group, that is isomorphic to one of the following: PSL(2, q), PSL(2, q) × Z2, SL(2, q) ×_{Z2} C, Â7, or SL(2, q) ×_{Z2} SL(2, q′), where C is solvable with a unique involution and q and q′ are odd prime powers greater than four. Which of these groups actually admit an action on a mod 2 homology 3-sphere, and which of them occur as isometry groups of a hyperbolic 3-manifold that is a 2-fold cyclic branched covering of a knot in S^3?

evidence.quote: Theorem 2.6. Let G be a finite non-solvable group of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of a mod 2 homology 3-sphere M, and let O(G) denote the maximal normal subgroup of odd order of G. Then G/O(G) has a normal subgroup (whose factor group is abelian or a 2-fold extension of an abelian group), isomorphic to one of the following groups: PSL(2, q) or PSL(2, q) × Z2, SL(2, q) ×Z2 C or Aˆ7, SL(2, q) ×Z2 SL(2, q′)

Problem 2.7: Which of the groups in Theorem 2.6 admit an action on a mod 2 homology 3-sphere? Which of them occur as isometry groups of a hyperbolic 3-manifold which is a 2-fold cyclic branched covering of a knot in S^3?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed orientable hyperbolic 3-manifold with non-solvable isometry group. Assume that whenever M is a p-fold cyclic branched covering of a knot K, the knot K is not strongly invertible but does have symmetric period p, meaning that K admits a cyclic symmetry of order p given by a periodic diffeomorphism h of (S^3, K) with nonempty connected fixed point set F disjoint from K, and the image of the 2-component link K ∪ F in the quotient S^3/h ≅ S^3 is a symmetric 2-component link whose two components are exchanged by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism. Find an upper bound on the number of such knots K and primes p, and determine the possible isometry groups of M.

evidence.quote: A knot K has symmetric period p if K has a cyclic symmetry of order p (a periodic diffeomorphism h of (S^3, K) with nonempty connected fixed point set F disjoint from K) such that the projection of the 2-component link K ∪ F to the quotient S^3/h ∼= S^3 gives a symmetric 2-component link K¯∪F¯ in S^3, i.e. there is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of S^3/h exchanging its two components.

Problem 2.9: Let M be a closed orientable hyperbolic 3-manifold with non-solvable isometry group. Suppose that every knot K such that M is a p-fold cyclic branched covering of K is not strongly invertible but has symmetric period p. Find an upper bound on the number of such knots K and primes p. What are the possible isometry groups of such a 3-manifold M?

accepted.question_text: For a hyperbolic 3-manifold M, how many distinct primes can occur as orders of hyperelliptic isometries of M, where hyperelliptic means that the quotient is S^3? Is there a uniform upper bound on the number of such primes? Which non-solvable groups can occur as isometry groups of such a hyperelliptic hyperbolic 3-manifold?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.10: How many different primes can occur as the orders of hyperelliptic isometries (i.e., with quotient S^3) of a hyperbolic 3-manifold M? Is there an upper bound on the number of such primes? What are the possible (non-solvable) isometry groups of such a hyperelliptic 3-manifold M?
